title: Regeneration of the load-bearing tendon–bone enthesis

concept.text: The innovation would regenerate the enthesis: the specialized attachment through which a tendon or ligament transfers force into bone. A successful treatment would rebuild a continuous transition in collagen organization, mineral content and cell phenotype, including unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage, and restore its ability to carry physiological loads. The goal is a functioning biological interface, beyond simply reconnecting tissue to bone or increasing tendon thickness.

The attachment solves a difficult mechanical problem: joining compliant soft tissue to much stiffer bone without concentrating damaging stresses at the junction. Its function depends on architecture across multiple scales as well as its mineral gradient. In the adult repairs described by the supplied review, healing generally produces scar and does not recreate this native organization. This is a documented limitation of ordinary healing and the interventions reviewed, rather than proof that regeneration is biologically impossible.

Rotator cuff repair and ligament attachment repair are appropriate applications. Other tendon-to-bone repairs, including Achilles attachment injuries, would require evidence specific to their anatomy and loading. The capability concerns restoration of the insertion itself; success at one attachment would not establish equivalent regeneration at every tendon or ligament attachment.

significance.text: Restoring the enthesis would address a central limitation of biological reattachment: scar can reconnect tissues without recovering the native mechanisms that distribute force between them. If regeneration recovered those mechanisms and sustained them under repeated loading, it could make repaired attachments more durable and reduce retears, graft failures and revisions attributable to insertion failure. The revolutionary capability would be recovery of a mechanically competent tissue transition after injury.

The benefit would depend on the whole repair surviving long enough for regeneration to occur. The 2024 review emphasizes early failures in which sutures pull out of repaired tendon during the days immediately after surgery. Regenerating the eventual attachment would therefore need to be combined with adequate early fixation and protection. It would not automatically eliminate failures caused by poor tendon quality, muscle dysfunction or other parts of the repair construct.

Conditional downstream possibility: reliable enthesis regeneration could change some reconstruction strategies and allow biological reattachment in situations where current healing is inadequate. Converting many reconstructions into repairs would additionally require sufficient viable tissue, suitable injury geometry and appropriate muscle function. Native-equivalent lifetime durability would require long-term evidence; neither outcome follows merely from restoring a graded interface in an experimental model.

Scope distinction: scarless healing within tendon midsubstance, adhesion-free gliding of an intrasynovial flexor tendon and reversal of fatty muscle degeneration remain separate capabilities. They may be needed alongside enthesis regeneration for full recovery in particular injuries. A collagen patch that increases tendon thickness or improves some repair outcomes does not, by those observations alone, establish regeneration of the native attachment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is coordinated regeneration of a graded attachment with native-like mechanical function. Producing fibrocartilage, depositing mineral or improving histological appearance individually is insufficient: the regenerated tissue must organize its composition, collagen structure and cellular transition so that these features work together to transfer load. The 2024 review identifies incomplete restoration of this microscale organization as a persistent gap.

The biological and engineering challenge is to translate local stimulation into a spatially organized, mature interface. Hedgehog stimulation, growth-factor combinations and progenitor-cell approaches described in the review offer components of that strategy, but the reported small-animal improvements did not fully restore intact structural and material properties. A successful intervention must coordinate where different tissues form and how they become mechanically integrated, rather than treating increased tissue formation as sufficient evidence of regeneration.

Translation also requires the attachment to develop while exposed to a clinically realistic healing environment. Early fixation must withstand the vulnerable interval, and the mature interface must tolerate physiological loading and repeated cycles without progressive damage. Demonstrating adequate strength, toughness and cyclic durability is a separate requirement from showing a mineral gradient or a favorable tissue section.

Translational synthesis: a human treatment would need reproducible delivery and maturation across the patient and injury populations it claims to serve. Age, tissue availability, chronic damage and the condition of the muscle–tendon unit could constrain its usefulness. Human assessment also needs a credible way to connect imaging evidence of the graded insertion with function, since destructive mechanical testing is unsuitable for successful clinical repairs and revision tissue is available only from a selected subset of patients.

current_state.text: Bousso, Genin and Thomopoulos's 2024 review in Current Opinion in Biomedical Engineering, published on 22 May 2024 as volume 31, article 100547, describes scar-mediated adult tendon-to-bone healing and states that no tissue-engineered technology had fully reconstituted the enthesis. It discusses small-animal advances involving Hedgehog stimulation, growth-factor combinations and progenitor cells, while reporting that structural and material properties remained below intact controls. These findings establish partial progress and a documented gap at the review's evidence date.

For clinical context, that review reports rotator cuff retearing in 20% of young patients and up to 94% of elderly patients, drawing on earlier literature. These are attributed historical figures, not a universal contemporary risk estimate or a prediction for an individual patient. The underlying studies were not independently supplied or inspected in the provided review, so their populations, procedures and follow-up conditions cannot be independently reconciled here.

The Regeneten systematic review by Marouane Benthami Kbibi, Filip Verhaegen and Philippe Debeer appeared in the December 2024 issue of Acta Orthopaedica Belgica and was published online on 24 January 2025. Its literature search ended on 6 June 2024. It reports reduced retears in some studies, while clinical outcomes remained within the range reported after traditional rotator cuff repair. This supports potential benefits of collagen implant augmentation, but does not demonstrate restoration of the continuous structural, mineral and cellular gradients required by this concept.

Interpretation of the Regeneten findings is limited by predominantly case-series evidence, only two randomized controlled trials, heterogeneity and widespread industry relationships, as identified in the supplied review. Different retear figures across the two reviews concern different evidence contexts and do not by themselves establish a contradiction. Neither improved integrity nor ordinary-range clinical scores resolve whether a native-like enthesis has regenerated.

The supplied evidence review assessed the full text of the 2024 enthesis manuscript and the full Regeneten article PDF. The Regeneten landing page provided only partial article content, although it confirmed the authors and online publication date. Figures were not inspected for the enthesis assessment; the conclusions used here rest on textual evidence. The separately supplied journal cover, contents and editorial-board documents do not supply scientific evidence for regeneration.

Evidence-date limitation: the supplied record contains no later freshness assessment establishing the field's status through 1 November 2026. Retrieval of these sources on that date does not update their scientific coverage. Whether a human graded insertion carrying physiological load had subsequently been demonstrated remains unresolved; the supplied evidence neither establishes such an achievement nor rules out later progress.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed structural demonstration: first establish in a large-animal tendon-to-bone repair model a continuous transition in mineral content, collagen organization and cell phenotype, including unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage. The assessment should distinguish organized regeneration from scar thickening or isolated mineral deposition. These are proposed criteria grounded in the interface's documented structure and function, rather than an established consensus completion standard.
completion_criteria.label: Large-animal repair regenerates a continuous graded insertion including fibrocartilage

completion_criteria.text: Proposed preclinical functional demonstration: compare regenerated attachments with matched intact attachments and appropriate repair controls for strength, toughness, cyclic durability and failure location. Failure outside the insertion would be useful supporting evidence, since native adult rupture tends to occur in the tendon midsubstance, but would not suffice on its own: a weak construct can fail elsewhere without recovering native-like mechanics. Destructive testing belongs in preclinical assessment.
completion_criteria.label: Attachment mechanics are benchmarked against intact and repair controls

completion_criteria.text: Proposed human demonstration: conduct controlled rotator cuff or ligament repair studies with predefined repair-integrity or graft-failure endpoints at two years, alongside functional outcomes and validated imaging capable of supporting assessment of the graded insertion. Compare outcomes with appropriate repair controls. An age-matched intact-tissue incident-injury benchmark could provide additional context where meaningfully defined; intact tendons do not have a postoperative retear rate. Two years is a proposed evaluation interval and would not establish lifetime durability.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled human studies assess two-year repair integrity and function

completion_criteria.text: Proposed structural confirmation in humans should combine validated imaging with tissue obtained at clinically indicated revision when available. Revision specimens are selected samples and cannot represent every successful repair. Greater tendon thickness on MRI, without evidence of the graded insertion, would not meet the structural goal. The imaging and tissue measures should be linked to demonstrated load-bearing performance rather than interpreted as interchangeable substitutes for function.
completion_criteria.label: Human graded insertion confirmation links structural evidence with load-bearing performance

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundaries: independently reproduce structural and functional results, report early fixation failures as well as later insertion failures, and define the anatomy, injury types, patient characteristics and rehabilitation conditions in which benefit has been demonstrated. Evidence from one attachment or a finite set of patient groups establishes demonstrated breadth within those conditions, not universal regeneration across all tendon and ligament insertions.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reproduction reports failure modes and demonstrated benefit boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ORT-01, Adult epimorphic regeneration of a functional limb, would require functional integration of multiple tissues, potentially including regenerated tendon–bone attachments. ORT-04 addresses one specialized interface within that much broader goal. ORT-06, Force-bearing skeletal muscle after volumetric muscle loss, concerns restoration of force-producing tissue; ORT-04 concerns transfer of force into bone. ORT-07, Meaningful motor and sensory recovery across long peripheral-nerve gaps, concerns neural connectivity. Restoring attachment, muscle force and neural control could be complementary, but success in any one does not establish the others.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-02, Biological restoration of the osteoarthritic synovial joint, and ORT-05, Restoration of the intervertebral disc as a living load-bearing organ, share the need to regenerate organized tissues that function under load. Their anatomical targets and functional endpoints differ from a tendon–bone insertion. Enthesis regeneration would not by itself restore an osteoarthritic joint or a degenerated disc.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-08, Anatomically precise and reversible control of osteogenesis, overlaps with the need to position mineralized tissue correctly, but controlled bone formation alone does not supply the enthesis's collagen, fibrocartilage and cellular gradients. ORT-09, Regeneration of a functioning growth plate, also concerns a spatially organized cartilage–bone system, but its defining function is longitudinal growth. ORT-10, Single-episode restoration of segmental long bone by vascularized, remodelable bone, addresses replacement of missing bone segments rather than restoration of the soft-tissue attachment to bone.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-03, Eradication of mature biofilm in bone and on orthopedic implants without removing the reconstruction, concerns infection control while preserving an existing reconstruction. That capability could support recovery in an infected repair, but biofilm clearance does not regenerate an enthesis, and successful enthesis regeneration does not establish eradication of infection. The two remain distinct clinical and biological goals.

change_log.change: Preserved ORT-04 and its title while expanding the concept into a structural and functional account of the graded attachment.
change_log.reason: Both research and review identify continuous mineral, collagen and cellular organization, together with load transfer, as the core innovation.

change_log.change: Qualified the adult healing problem as the documented behavior of ordinary repair and reviewed interventions.
change_log.reason: Failure to regenerate in the supplied evidence does not establish biological impossibility under every intervention.

change_log.change: Replaced guaranteed original durability and broad conversion of reconstructions into repairs with conditional consequences.
change_log.reason: Long-term durability, viable tissue, injury geometry, muscle condition and other repair limitations require separate evidence.

change_log.change: Added early tissue–suture failure and protection during healing to the account of practical barriers.
change_log.reason: The supplied review identifies early suture pullout, limiting the inference that eventual interface regeneration alone would prevent overall repair failure.

change_log.change: Preserved the 20% and up-to-94% retear figures with attribution and historical context.
change_log.reason: The review reports them, but the underlying studies were not independently assessed and the figures are not universal contemporary risk estimates.

change_log.change: Restored the Regeneten authors and distinguished its December 2024 issue date, 24 January 2025 online publication and 6 June 2024 search cutoff.
change_log.reason: The supplied review recovered the byline and dates, correcting the earlier extraction note and clarifying evidence coverage.

change_log.change: Integrated Regeneten study limitations and separated augmentation outcomes from evidence of enthesis regeneration.
change_log.reason: Reduced retears in some studies and ordinary-range clinical outcomes do not demonstrate reconstruction of the native graded interface.

change_log.change: Dated the documented gap and left field status through 1 November 2026 unresolved.
change_log.reason: The supplied freshness record is empty; retrieval date cannot substitute for later scientific evidence.

change_log.change: Revised completion criteria to separate preclinical destructive testing from human assessment and to include strength, toughness and cyclic durability.
change_log.reason: Failure outside the insertion alone is insufficient, and destructive mechanical testing is inappropriate for successful human repairs.

change_log.change: Replaced comparison with intact-tendon postoperative retear rates with repair controls and an optional, meaningfully defined incident-injury benchmark.
change_log.reason: Intact tendons have incident injuries rather than postoperative retears.

change_log.change: Explicitly treated the two-year interval, staged demonstrations and reproducibility requirements as proposals, and identified revision-sampling limitations.
change_log.reason: These are proposed evidentiary criteria rather than consensus standards; revision tissue is selectively available.

change_log.change: Added distinctions with every other supplied roster entry and preserved adjacent tendon and muscle problems as separate capabilities.
change_log.reason: Related regenerative goals may complement ORT-04 without sharing its identity or completion endpoint.

unresolved_issues: Whether later work demonstrated a human graded, physiologically load-bearing enthesis by 1 November 2026 cannot be determined from the supplied record.

The underlying studies behind the age-associated 20% and up-to-94% retear figures were not independently assessed, leaving their applicability to particular contemporary repair populations unresolved.
The supplied evidence does not establish which intervention can reproducibly restore both graded organization and intact-like mechanical performance in humans.
Human imaging measures that convincingly establish the relevant structural gradients and their relationship to mechanical competence remain to be specified and validated.
Acceptable mechanical equivalence margins, clinical effect sizes and a meaningful intact-tissue incident-injury benchmark require prospective definition; none is established by the supplied review.

The durability of any regenerated attachment beyond the proposed two-year clinical interval, and its performance across different anatomical sites and patient populations, would require further evidence.
How best to protect the early repair while permitting functional maturation, and how much benefit remains when muscle degeneration or poor tendon quality limits recovery, remain unresolved.

brief.title: Regrowing the attachment between tendon and bone
possible: After a shoulder tendon tear or ligament injury, people could regrow a living attachment that carries everyday loads. Treatment would restore the gradual transition from soft tissue to hard bone, including its changing fibers, minerals and cells.
why: Scar can reconnect tissue to bone without restoring the structure that spreads force safely across the join. Regrowing that structure could make repairs more durable, reduce repeat tears and graft failures, and spare patients further surgery.

sources.who: Ismael Bousso, Guy Genin and Stavros Thomopoulos
sources.showed: Their review describes how the enthesis, the tendon–bone attachment, spreads force and why scar fails to restore it. Animal treatments improved healing without fully recovering healthy structure and mechanical performance.
sources.quote: The healing process produces scar tissue and poor mechanical behavior, rather than regenerating a healthy enthesis
sources.cited_for: Restoring the attachment requires coordinated tissue structure and the ability to carry loads.
sources.not_established: The reviewed treatments did not fully rebuild an attachment with the structure and mechanical performance of healthy tissue.

sources.who: Marouane Benthami Kbibi, Filip Verhaegen and Philippe Debeer
sources.showed: Their review found fewer repeat tears in some studies using Regeneten, a collagen protein patch, for shoulder tendon repair. Clinical outcomes remained within the range of traditional repair.
sources.quote: In 1 randomised trial, the retear rate was significantly lower in the implant group compared to the control group.
sources.cited_for: A patch can improve some repair outcomes without demonstrating regeneration of the attachment.
sources.not_established: Thicker tendons and fewer tears do not establish restoration of the gradual transition in fibers, minerals and cells.

shown: Bousso and colleagues describe partial progress in small animals using cells and signals that stimulate tissue growth. The repaired attachments still fell short of intact tissue in structure and mechanical performance.
missing: A regenerated attachment must coordinate changing fibers, minerals and cells, including tough cushioning tissue called fibrocartilage.
The attachment must withstand everyday forces and repeated loading without progressive damage.
A human treatment must reliably mature into a functioning attachment while the early repair remains protected.
Human scans must reliably reveal the tissue transition and connect it to the attachment’s ability to carry loads.

milestones.label: Large animals regrow the full tissue transition
milestones.explanation: Large-animal repairs would have to restore continuous changes in minerals, collagen protein fibers and cell types, including fibrocartilage with and without mineral. This would distinguish organized regrowth from scar.

milestones.label: Regrown attachments withstand mechanical testing
milestones.explanation: Animal tests would have to compare strength, resistance to tearing, repeated loading and failure location against intact attachments and repair controls. This would establish how well the new tissue carries force.

milestones.label: Controlled human studies demonstrate durable repair and function
milestones.explanation: Controlled human studies would have to assess repair survival and function over two years, using validated scans to assess the tissue transition. This would test patient benefit against standard repairs.

milestones.label: Human tissue structure connects to load-bearing performance
milestones.explanation: Validated scans and tissue from medically needed repeat surgery, when available, would have to confirm the transition and connect it to load-bearing performance. This would link structural regrowth to function in people.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results and define benefit boundaries
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce structural and functional results, reporting early and late failures across defined injuries, patients and rehabilitation conditions. This would establish where treatment works.

uncertain: Which treatment can reliably restore both the organized tissue transition and healthy mechanical performance in humans?
How closely must a regenerated attachment match healthy tissue to count as success?
How long will benefits last, and how will damaged muscle or poor tendon quality limit recovery?

page.title: Fibrocartilaginous enthesis regeneration
page.definition: An injured enthesis, the attachment of a tendon or ligament to bone, regenerates its graded collagen, mineral and cell organization, including unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage (cartilage-like connective tissue), and transfers physiological loads through the restored insertion.

goal.need: Sutures and bone anchors can reattach a torn tendon, but scar at the attachment lacks the native transition that distributes load and resists tearing. After repair of posterosuperior rotator cuff tears, 844 of 3,350 repairs (25%) had torn again on imaging at a median of 18 months. Restoring that transition could reduce repeat tears and help preserve strength. The benefit for symptoms is less certain: average differences in pain and shoulder scores between healed and retorn repairs were below commonly used thresholds for clinical importance.

figures.caption: Approximate elastic moduli of the tissues joined by the enthesis
figures.note: Elastic modulus measures material stiffness. These are order-of-magnitude values, not regeneration thresholds.

statements.body: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, Biologic Treatment of Orthopaedic Injuries symposium
statements.quote: Tendon-to-bone healing is critical for successful surgical treatment of soft-tissue injuries.
statements.context: The symposium report identifies rotator cuff reattachment as a clinically relevant model and discusses biological augmentation of tendon-to-bone healing.

statements.body: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, Innovative Treatments for Enthesis Repair roundtable
statements.quote: develop regenerative strategies for enhanced tendon-to-bone healing in the adult setting.
statements.context: The participants’ 2018 report links this goal to understanding how a gradient of cells and extracellular matrix forms at the attachment.

completion.title: Human regeneration restores a graded enthesis that transfers physiological loads.
completion.criterion: Human evidence demonstrates regeneration of the tendon- or ligament-to-bone transition, including unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage and gradients in collagen organization, mineral content and cell phenotype, together with transfer of physiological loads through that regenerated insertion. Structural and functional evidence must concern the same intervention and attachment site. MRI continuity, tendon thickening or improved clinical scores alone do not satisfy this test.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body defining a combined human structural and physiological-loading test was located.
completion.basis: The Atlas combines two properties of the native attachment: a graded fibrocartilaginous insertion and transfer of physiological loads through it. Human ACL revision biopsies showed four zones in patellar tendon grafts that healed by bone plug incorporation. Such a graft brings a pre-existing tendon-to-bone junction. Its histology alone establishes neither the formation of a new junction nor the loads that junction carries.

milestones.title: An injured attachment forms fibrocartilage connecting soft tissue to bone in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: After injury in an animal model, histology shows newly formed fibrocartilage connecting tendon or ligament to bone at the repair site. Evidence of both unmineralized and mineralized zones is unnecessary at this stage.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; AAOS, ASTM and enthesis-method searches yielded no common histological pass score. The cited experiments supply case-specific evidence, not a consensus regeneration threshold.

milestones.title: A large-animal repaired attachment exceeds suture repair in failure load at 12 weeks.
milestones.criterion: At 12 weeks after large-animal repair, tensile testing shows a greater load to failure for the treated attachment than for direct suture repair at the same site (P < 0.05). The study includes an intact attachment comparator.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback based on Chen et al.’s canine infraspinatus experiment. No outside body was identified that sets this combination of time point, comparators and superiority threshold across attachment sites. The quoted cutoff is the experiment’s statistical rule.
milestones.threshold_quote: A value of P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

milestones.title: A regenerative attachment treatment is administered to a person under an authorised clinical protocol.
milestones.criterion: At least one person receives an intervention under an authorised clinical protocol that identifies healing or regeneration of the tendon- or ligament-to-bone attachment as an intended effect. The treatment record identifies the attachment site.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback for the general capability; searches found no cross-anatomy enthesis-regeneration entry criterion for human studies. Yoon et al. report a rotator cuff-specific protocol approved by South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.

milestones.title: A randomized human study improves attachment integrity and validated joint function.
milestones.criterion: A randomized human trial shows superiority over its control on both a prespecified measure of repair integrity and a validated joint-function measure. For rotator cuff protocol NCT02484950, the primary measure is the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score at one year, and the structural measure is repair integrity on one-year MRI. For another attachment, the trial must prespecify measures appropriate to that site.
milestones.set_by: Rush University Medical Center, NCT02484950 protocol amended on 19 April 2021. These endpoints were written for rotator cuff repair; other attachment sites require their own registered structural and functional endpoints.
milestones.threshold_quote: there will be improved clinical outcomes and reduced incidence of recurrent structural defects

milestones.title: An injured human attachment regrows the graded fibrocartilaginous insertion.
milestones.criterion: Human evidence identifies both unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage at the repaired insertion, with spatial transitions in collagen organization, mineral content and cell phenotype. It distinguishes newly formed interface tissue from scar, surviving native insertion and a junction transplanted with a graft.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; searches of society reports, standards, trial protocols and human regeneration studies found no accepted test confirming the complete regenerated human insertion.

milestones.title: A repaired animal attachment develops the four zones of a fibrocartilaginous insertion.
milestones.criterion: Histology at the repaired animal insertion shows four contiguous zones in order: tendon or ligament, unmineralized fibrocartilage, mineralized fibrocartilage and bone. The evidence identifies the transition as newly formed at the repair site.
milestones.set_by: The four-zone histological convention for a chondral insertion, described in human graft biopsies and applied to experimental tendon-to-bone attachments.
milestones.threshold_quote: The chondral insertion of the graft to the bone is composed of four characteristic zones.

not_found: No outside definition of completed human enthesis regeneration combining graded structure with physiological load transfer was found.
No accepted mechanical equivalence margin, cyclic-load requirement, cycle count or follow-up duration for this capability was found.
No human publication demonstrating both the specified regenerated structure and its physiological load transfer was located for any listed attachment site.
No society or programme statement disputing the value or feasibility of regenerating the human fibrocartilaginous enthesis was located.

results.finding: Rabbit rotator cuff histology (n=11 scaffold-treated repairs) showed fibrocartilage joining tendon to bone at 4 weeks.
results.detail: The suture-only repairs showed absent fibrocartilage and disrupted tendon-to-bone continuity.
results.quote: Further, in vivo, the BMS promoted successful integrative healing, forming distinct tendon, fibrocartilage, and bone regions at the repair site.

results.finding: Rabbit rotator cuff histology (n=11 scaffold-treated repairs) identified 3 regions at the repaired insertion.
results.detail: The histology used decalcified sections. Micro-CT quantified bone remodeling and did not establish a separate mineralized fibrocartilage zone.
results.quote: The (+) BMS group shows well-organized tissue architecture with distinct tendon, fibrocartilage, and bone layers, indicating successful integration and zonal regeneration in young rabbits.

results.finding: After ACL reconstruction, all 5 mice examined at 4 weeks had fibrocartilage linking the tendon graft to bone in both tunnels.
results.quote: They continued to mature the attachments yielding zonal insertion sites at 4 weeks with collagen fibers spanning across unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage and anchored to the adjacent bone.

results.finding: After ACL reconstruction, all 5 mice examined at 4 weeks had four-zone graft-to-bone insertions in both tunnels.
results.detail: The four-zone transition formed where the tail tendon autograft integrated with bone in the reconstruction tunnels.
results.quote: They continued to mature the attachments yielding zonal insertion sites at 4 weeks with collagen fibers spanning across unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage and anchored to the adjacent bone.

results.finding: Rat Achilles repairs with adhesive formed a continuous fibrocartilaginous insertion by 12 weeks (histology n = 9/group).
results.detail: Suture-only repairs showed disorganized fibrocartilage with poor structural continuity.
results.quote: A well-defined PG gradient spanning bone-to-tendon was consistently observed. The spatial distribution of PG staining suggested a more organized fibrocartilaginous transition zone in the adhesive-treated interfaces.

results.finding: Adhesive-augmented rat Achilles repairs showed a nascent four-zone insertion at four weeks (histology n = 9/group).
results.detail: The paper describes a native-like architecture with incomplete restoration of native morphology.
results.quote: At four weeks, a nascent transition zone containing bone, mineralized cartilage, unmineralized cartilage, and tendon was evident

results.finding: Adhesive-augmented rat Achilles repairs showed no significant failure-load advantage (P > 0.05, n = 11/repair group, n = 6 intact).
results.detail: Area-normalized ultimate stress was higher with adhesive augmentation (P < 0.001). The criterion specifies whole-construct failure load.
results.quote: At the whole-construct level, ultimate load, displacement, and stiffness did not differ significantly among the suture, suture + adhesive, and intact groups (85.36 N (SD 21.22), 88.24 N (SD 16.10), and 81.87 N (SD 11.43); p > 0.05)

results.finding: All 46 patients allocated to concentrated bone marrow aspirate received it at the repaired supraspinatus insertion.
results.detail: The trial randomized 91 patients under protocol NCT02484950.

results.finding: In 91 randomized rotator cuff patients, 75 had one-year MRI. Marrow concentrate reduced retears by 39 percentage points.
results.detail: The MRI analysis excluded two patients per group who required revision repair within one year.
results.quote:
On 1-year MRI,
evidence of rotator cuff retear was identified in just 18% of
patients in the cBMA group versus 57% in the control
group.

results.finding: In the 30-person ACL reconstruction trial, 17 completers received PRP or BMAC plus PRP at both graft-to-bone attachment sites.
results.detail: The Kaohsiung Medical University Hospital IRB approved the protocol (KMUHIRB-F(I)-20170122, NCT05191732).
results.quote: In this study, PRP or BMAC + PRP gel was applied at both ends of the tendon graft, and then PRP solution or BMAC + PRP mixture was intraarticularly injected.

results.finding: Among ACL trial completers (n = 27), BMAC plus PRP improved laxity versus control (P = 0.029), with no significant functional-score or MRI healing benefit.
results.detail: The 24-week femoral tunnel widening was in the unfavorable direction for the MRI measure of interface healing.
results.quote: The Lysholm and IKDC scores improved with time in all three groups. No significant difference was observed in the functional score at different time points among all groups.

results.finding: Canine infraspinatus histology (n = 5 per repair group) showed fibrocartilage bridging tendon to bone, with 68.40% of regenerated tissue in the graft group resembling native enthesis.
results.detail: The surgeon removed residual native fibrocartilage from the footprint. The suture-only group also formed enthesis-like tissue, providing evidence of new interface formation without implanted fibrocartilage.
results.quote: Histologically, newly-formed bone at the footprint of IT and structurally integrated well with the ruptured infraspinatus tendon by a fibrous or/and fibrocartilaginous tissue in all groups

results.finding: Canine infraspinatus histology (n = 5 per repair group) found native-like tendon, fibrocartilage and bone in 68.40% of the graft group's regenerated tissue.
results.detail: The mineral mapping that distinguished calcified from uncalcified fibrocartilage was performed on the decellularized scaffold and native tissue.
results.quote: According to blinded evaluations, 68.40% of the regenerated tissue in the TE group is histologically similar to the native enthesis of the INT group, which comprised of well-orientated fibrous connective tissue (tendon), fibrocartilaginous tissue, and subchondral bone (mix of lamella and woven bones)

results.finding: Canine infraspinatus graft repair (n = 8 per group) exceeded direct suture in tensile failure load (P = 0.0002).
results.detail: Six graft specimens failed at the insertion and two at the tendon midsubstance. All direct-suture and intact specimens failed at the insertion.
results.quote:
At postoperative week 12, the specimens (n = 8/group) in the CTL or EG groups recovered about 53.67% and 77.42% of the failure load (N) compared with the INT group, and the EG group presented significantly larger value in failure load than the CTL group (
P
= 0.0002)

results.finding: Sheep rotator cuff repairs (n = 5 per arm for histology) showed a newly formed fibrocartilaginous tendon-to-bone attachment at 12 weeks with scaffold augmentation.
results.quote: In the majority of these animals treated with the scaffold, prominent perforating collagen fibers, similar to Sharpey fibers, were present and extending through a region of calcified fibrocartilage and attaching to the humeral footprint.

results.finding: Sheep rotator cuff repairs (n = 5 per arm for histology) showed uncalcified and calcified fibrocartilage at 12 weeks.
results.quote: In addition, and not unsurprisingly for these time points, the organization of the zones of the enthesis (uncalcified and calcified fibrocartilage) is thinner and less prominent than that observed in a normal control animal.

results.finding: At 12 weeks, scaffold-augmented sheep rotator cuff repairs had a 599.77 N higher mean failure load than unaugmented repairs (n = 5 per arm).
results.detail: The reported P < .01 applies to the scaffold group's increase from week 6 to week 12. The 599.77 N difference is calculated from the reported means.
results.quote: At the 12-week point, the mean ultimate failure force was 1846.77 ± 431.96 N for the nanofiber treatment vs. 1247.00 ± 1122.42 N for the control (no scaffold).

results.finding: Cell-treated rat Achilles repairs (n=4 per group at each time point) formed fibrocartilage at the tendon–bone junction by day 45.
results.quote: In contrast, a homogeneous collagen II- and GAG-rich matrix covered the bone at the tendon insertion in the cell-injected rat (h, i).

results.finding: MSC-treated rat Achilles repairs (n=4 per group) showed native-like chondrocyte columns at day 45.
results.detail: The histology score assessed type II collagen, glycosaminoglycans and chondrocyte organization without mapping a mineralization boundary.

results.finding: Rat Achilles repairs with MSCs (n=6–8 per group) reached a mean failure load of 84.6 N, significantly above suture repair alone.
results.detail: Six intact insertions were tested. Specimens that failed in the tendon were excluded from the mechanical analysis.
results.quote: Cell injection significantly improved healing (69%, p = 0.0028 for G2 and p = 0.006 for G3) and the load-to-failure after 45 days (p<0.05) over controls.

results.finding: In a 6-patient Achilles rupture series, 1 patient with a documented calcaneal insertion rupture received cell therapy under compassionate use.
results.detail: The methods describe intratendinous and peritendinous delivery. The ethics statement describes a hospital exemption for chronic tendinopathy.
results.quote:
All patients tolerated local administration of 20 × 10 6 
aBM-MSCs into the Achilles tendon without complications.

results.finding: In a 6-patient Achilles rupture series with MRI follow-up, the median VISA-A score improved by 86.5 points.
results.detail: The VISA-A change is pooled across the case series, which included ruptures at different locations.
results.quote:
and their VISA-A score had increased markedly 
by the last visit (median VISA-A score difference was 86.5 
(68.0 – 94.0) points).

results.finding: MRI showed tendon-fiber continuity at 12 months in 1 patient treated for a chronic partial Achilles rupture at the calcaneal insertion.
results.detail: The reported regeneration endpoint was an MRI score. No tissue analysis characterized the repaired interface.
results.quote:
Case 4 (64 years old) – initially diagnosed with partial 
chronic insertional ATR at the calcaneus level– showed 
clear continuity of tendon tissue fibers at insertion, absence 
of peritendinous and Kager’s fat edema at 12 months, and 
complete tendon regeneration at 24 months.

results.finding: In an ethics-approved rotator cuff trial, 15 patients received dermal allograft bridging to promote healing at the greater tuberosity.
results.detail: Research ethics board approval No. 1015440. One reconstruction patient did not complete follow-up.
results.quote:
The patients
randomized to the reconstruction group underwent maxi-
mal repair performed along with a rotator cuff reconstruc-
tion using a dermal allograft tissue (GraftJacket; Wright
Medical) as described by the senior author (I.W.) previ-
ously49 (Figure 2).

results.finding: In 29 analyzed rotator cuff patients, dermal allograft bridging reduced MRI-confirmed complete retears versus maximal repair (P < .001).
results.detail: MRI was planned for 12 months and obtained at a mean of 1.21 years after reconstruction and 1.22 years after maximal repair.
results.quote:
The reconstruction group had 3 of 14 (21%) patients
with complete retears, whereas the repair group had 13 of
15 (87%) patients with complete retears. The difference
between the 2 groups was statistically significant ( P \
.001).

results.finding: In 36 beagles, scaffold-treated rotator cuff repairs showed more cartilaginous matrix at the tendon–bone interface through 24 weeks.
results.detail: The native cartilage layer on the bone side was removed before repair. The report describes regeneration of a cartilage layer, with no explicit histological identification of a continuous fibrocartilage bridge.
results.quote: Furthermore, Safranin O‐Fast Green staining revealed a higher abundance of cartilaginous matrix components in the UC group.

results.finding: Canine rotator cuff repairs in a 36-beagle study had a significantly higher 12-week mean failure load with scaffold augmentation, by 98.6 N.
results.detail: The 98.6 N difference is calculated from the reported group means. The 36 beagles were divided among three follow-up cohorts. The text gives no separate sample count for the 12-week tensile test.
results.quote: the UC group exhibited improved mechanical strength and outperformed the control group (87.4 ± 26.5 vs 186.0 ± 42.9 N, P < 0.01

results.finding: In a 20-patient trial, 10 patients received an umbilical cord scaffold at the rotator cuff attachment under an ethics-approved protocol.
results.quote: the experimental group received an additional patch implantation at the site of the TBI before fixation.

results.finding: In 20 randomized rotator cuff patients, scaffold augmentation improved early interface MRI grade (P < 0.01).
results.detail: The reported trial was ChiCTR2100050630. Its published outcomes cover MRI at 12 and 24 weeks.
results.quote: early healing was confirmed at 12 weeks (P < 0.01).

results.finding: Goat patellar tendon repair with articular cartilage interposition (36 grafted knees) yielded 69.10% fibrocartilage transition-zone regeneration at 24 weeks.
results.detail: The 36 knees were in the grafted group. The excerpt gives neither the 24-week sample size nor the histological observations used to score regeneration.
results.quote: Autologous articular cartilage interposition resulted in more fibrocartilage transition zone regeneration (69.10% ± 14.11% [mean ± standard deviation] versus 8.67% ± 7.01% at 24 weeks) than direct repair at all times.

results.finding: In a study of 16 chickens, light microscopy showed fibrocartilage connecting the repaired deep flexor tendon to bone at 8 weeks.
results.detail: The sample size is for the full study. The text gives no separate count for the 8-week time point. The fibrocartilage layer was visible by light microscopy and went undetected by scanning electron microscopy.
results.quote:
The point of insertion of the re-anchored tendon was made of three layers, con
sisting of tendon, fibrocartilage and bone, 8 weeks after the operation, similar to the 
normal anchorage.

results.finding: In six paired canine rotator cuff repairs, augmentation increased 12-week tensile failure load by 35% over suture repair alone.
results.detail: Testing measured the whole repair construct, including the retained tendon and augmentation device. Failures began in soft tissue, and the precise failure site was indeterminate.
results.quote: At twelve weeks, the ultimate load of augmented repairs averaged 246 ± 143 N (35%) more than that of six unaugmented repairs (p = 0.009).

results.finding: Among 20 men with chronic proximal patellar tendinopathy, 10 received autologous bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell injections at the proximal insertion lesion.
results.quote: Of these, 10 participants were treated with BM-MSC (20 3 106 cells) and 10 with Lp-PRP.

results.finding: In a randomized trial of large rotator cuff tears (60 randomized, 43 followed), dermal allograft augmentation reduced MRI-confirmed retears to 9.1%.
results.detail: The final analysis included 22 patients with patch augmentation and 21 controls. Seventeen randomized patients were lost to follow-up.
results.quote: The retear rate was 9.1% in the allograft group, which was significantly lower than that in the control group (38.1%).

results.finding: After ACL reconstruction, preoperative exercise improved femoral graft–bone healing on 12-month MRI versus standard care (53 completers, p = 0.003).
results.detail: At 12 months, the femoral MRI grade and IKDC score favored exercise. Tibial MRI healing grade, Lysholm score, and KT-2000 laxity showed no significant between-group differences at that visit.
results.quote:
At 3, 6 and 12 months post-ACLR, femoral 
tendon-bone healing grades were significantly higher 
than that of CON group ( p = 0.02, 0.008, 0.003).

results.finding: Repaired sheep patellar tendon insertions (n = 6) showed four contiguous zones in every histological section examined.
results.detail: Some sections had a clear tidemark. The four zones remained identifiable across gradual transitions in the other sections.
results.quote: In all the specimens, a direct type enthesis was found with the characteristic transition between bone, mineralized fibrocartilage, demineralised fibrocartilage and tendon

results.finding: Rabbit subscapularis autograft repairs (n=2 shoulders examined histologically) showed a tidemark and columnar chondrocytes at 12 weeks.
results.detail: The histology was qualitative. The paper does not report how many repaired shoulders showed the tidemark.
results.quote: In the 12-week graft group, significant changes were observed in the tendon–bone junction region. A typical columnar arrangement of chondrocytes, along with the presence of the tidemark, was evident.

results.finding: In a 35-sheep ACL reconstruction study, tibial graft histology showed four contiguous insertion zones.
results.detail: The study reports 35 sheep across five postoperative time points. The supplied text does not specify the size of the 52-week subgroup.
results.quote:
At 1 year, a normal di-
rect ligament insertion with a transition zone consist-
ing of mineralized cartilage and ﬁbrocartilage was
found in all specimens distally and proximally.

goal.need = "Sutures and bone anchors can reattach a torn tendon, but scar at the attachment lacks the native transition that distributes load and resists tearing. After repair of posterosuperior rotator cuff tears, 844 of 3,350 repairs (25%) had torn again on imaging at a median of 18 months. Restoring that transition could reduce repeat tears and help preserve strength. The benefit for symptoms is less certain: average differences in pain and shoulder scores between healed and retorn repairs were below commonly used thresholds for clinical importance.". Reason: The current rationale quantifies the tissue stiffness difference but omits the frequency of retear and the limits of what better healing would mean for patients.

add statement by National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, Innovative Treatments for Enthesis Repair roundtable, 2017: "develop regenerative strategies for enhanced tendon-to-bone healing in the adult setting.". Reason: The published NIAMS roundtable report explicitly connects formation of the graded attachment to the goal of regenerative treatment in adults.

edit completion: basis = "The Atlas combines two properties of the native attachment: a graded fibrocartilaginous insertion and transfer of physiological loads through it. Human ACL revision biopsies showed four zones in patellar tendon grafts that healed by bone plug incorporation. Such a graft brings a pre-existing tendon-to-bone junction. Its histology alone establishes neither the formation of a new junction nor the loads that junction carries."; refs = [1, 2, 3, 4, 19, 20]. Reason: Human ACL revision biopsies provide a closer structural comparison than MRI continuity and explain why the origin of a four-zone insertion matters.
add case "Patellar tendon". Reason: The roundtable identifies the patellar tendon insertion as a distinct site for translational enthesis repair research.
add case "Flexor tendon". Reason: The roundtable identifies the flexor tendon insertion as a separate site of experimental tendon-to-bone repair.

edit m1: criterion = "After injury in an animal model, histology shows newly formed fibrocartilage connecting tendon or ligament to bone at the repair site. Evidence of both unmineralized and mineralized zones is unnecessary at this stage."; refs = [2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 14]. Reason: The animal histology criterion currently includes study dates, group sizes and results that belong with the evidence.

add milestone after m1: "A repaired animal attachment develops the four zones of a fibrocartilaginous insertion.". Reason: The existing animal milestones can both be met without demonstrating the organized fibrocartilage transition already identifiable in animal repair models.

edit m2: criterion = "At 12 weeks after large-animal repair, tensile testing shows a greater load to failure for the treated attachment than for direct suture repair at the same site (P < 0.05). The study includes an intact attachment comparator."; set_by = "Atlas fallback based on Chen et al.\u2019s canine infraspinatus experiment. No outside body was identified that sets this combination of time point, comparators and superiority threshold across attachment sites. The quoted cutoff is the experiment\u2019s statistical rule."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; refs = [7, 19]. Reason: The cited significance cutoff belongs to one canine experiment and supplies no registered or cross-site 12-week performance standard.

edit m3: criterion = "At least one person receives an intervention under an authorised clinical protocol that identifies healing or regeneration of the tendon- or ligament-to-bone attachment as an intended effect. The treatment record identifies the attachment site.". Reason: The human administration criterion mixes the act of treating a patient with subsequent safety and imaging results from a six-patient study.

edit m4: criterion = "A randomized human trial shows superiority over its control on both a prespecified measure of repair integrity and a validated joint-function measure. For rotator cuff protocol NCT02484950, the primary measure is the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score at one year, and the structural measure is repair integrity on one-year MRI. For another attachment, the trial must prespecify measures appropriate to that site.". Reason: The registered protocol distinguishes the primary shoulder score from the secondary structural outcome, while the current criterion mixes both with trial results.

edit m5: criterion = "Human evidence identifies both unmineralized and mineralized fibrocartilage at the repaired insertion, with spatial transitions in collagen organization, mineral content and cell phenotype. It distinguishes newly formed interface tissue from scar, surviving native insertion and a junction transplanted with a graft."; refs = [1, 2, 4, 19, 20]. Reason: The human structural criterion embeds a review count and a search verdict that can change independently of the histological test.
remove not found 3. Reason: The roundtable participants’ published account and the full texts of both the mouse ACL attachment study and the randomized human ACL interface study are accessible.

add not found: "No society or programme statement disputing the value or feasibility of regenerating the human fibrocartilaginous enthesis was located.". Reason: The society and roundtable documents discuss limitations of available models and outcome measures without taking a position against the goal itself.
